data.title: US hosts G20 'energy abundance' talks amid Iran war shock
data.description: HOUSTON, Texas - The United States on Monday kicks off a set of G20 meetings touting "energy abundance," even as President Donald Trump's war against Iran continues to disrupt global fuel markets.

data.title: South Korea aims to save seniors lost in digital age
data.description: SUWON (SOUTH KOREA) - A little cheer rose for 79-year-old Hwang Sun-hee after she managed to place an online order at a training session in South Korea, which has one of the world's starkest digital divides for seniors.

data.title: Polls open in Philippine Muslim enclave after deadly shooting
data.description: MARAWI (PHILIPPINES) - Voters across the Philippines' autonomous Muslim region began casting ballots for their first elected parliament Monday morning, hours after gun violence left at least three people dead outside a polling station.

data.title: Migrant workers flock to Indian Kashmir despite militant threats
data.description: SRINAGAR (INDIA) - Every spring, mason Mohammad Ghulam Sarwar boards a train to Indian Kashmir, seeking higher wages despite the risk of being targeted by militants in the disputed Himalayan region.

data.title: Canada's Carney seeks closer Europe ties to counter hostile US
data.description: MONTREAL (CANADA) - Prime Minister Mark Carney calls Canada "the most European of non-European countries," and while formal EU membership may be tricky, he is pursuing unprecedented closeness with the bloc to reduce dependence on a hostile United States.

data.title: 'Fed up': Thousands march against Sinaloa Cartel violence
data.description: CULIACáN (MEXICO) - Chanting and waving banners, thousands marched Sunday in the Mexican city of Culiacan to protest the deaths of people caught up in a war between two rival factions of the infamous Sinaloa Cartel.

data.title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launched over 50 strikes against them in 24 hours
data.description: SANAA - Yemen's Houthis said Sunday that Saudi Arabia had launched more than 50 strikes against their positions in 24 hours, after the Iran-backed group claimed a rare drone and missile attack on a military base in the kingdom.

data.title: DC's Kennedy Center faces bankruptcy, closure: media
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Leaders of the Kennedy Center who have sought to add President Donald Trump's name to the storied institution say it is facing bankruptcy and possible closure in days, the Washington Post reported Sunday.

data.title: Poland, Ukraine slam Russian strikes near border as 'escalation'
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Poland and Ukraine on Sunday denounced Russian strikes close to the Polish border, including on a Warsaw-bound train and near a frontier checkpoint -- as an "escalation" in the war.

data.title: Leftwing opposition seen leading Sweden election, far-right losing ground
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Sweden's left-wing parties led in Sunday's general election, according to two exit polls published after voting ended, with the far-right seen losing ground.

data.title: Dozens arrested in major anti-LGBTQ raids in Turkey
data.description: ISTANBUL - Turkish police on Sunday swooped on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists, arresting at least 60 people in raids authorities said were aimed at boosting traditional family values, officials and activists said.

data.title: Trump administration reluctant to slow AI, Democrats see urgent need
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump and key allies voiced opposition Sunday to drastically curbing the development of artificial intelligence, despite calls in recent days from leading industry figures to tap the brakes.

data.title: Trump turns to golf, family business on Irish visit's second day
data.description: DOONBEG (IRELAND) - Donald Trump turns his focus Sunday to golf and promoting his business interests, as he wraps up a two-day visit to Ireland during which his off-the-cuff diplomacy has caused another stir.

data.title: Iran's economic ties to Dubai hard to break despite war
data.description: DUBAI - In the markets of old Dubai, saffron, cumin, pistachios and almonds from Iran still fill the stalls, as if the two shores of the Gulf were not separated by war.

data.title: Macron, Carney to visit French islands after Trump's map post
data.description: PARIS - The leaders of France and Canada will next week visit France's North Atlantic territory of Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon to underscore their support for national borders in the face of Donald Trump's territorial ambitions, Paris said Sunday.

data.title: Philippine rescuers pull 41 more bodies from burned ferry
data.description: CORON, Philippines - The bodies of 41 victims of the worst Philippine ferry disaster in over a decade made their way through the blue waters of a resort area on Sunday, bound for a dock where forensic investigators awaited them.

data.title: Myanmar says UN envoy illegitimate ahead of credentials decision
data.description: YANGON - Myanmar's military-backed government said Sunday their UN ambassador -- loyal to ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi -- is occupying the office illegitimately, as the organisation prepares to weigh his replacement.

data.title: China, Russia, India seek economic cooperation at BRICS
data.description: NEW DELHI - BRICS leaders including China, Russia and India entered a second day of talks in New Delhi on Sunday, discussing "inclusive global growth", after reaching rare agreement calling for calm in the Middle East.

data.title: One dead, 102 rescued from stricken ferry off Indonesia's Java
data.description: JAKARTA - One person was killed and more than 100 were rescued on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the Indonesian islands of Java and Borneo was hit by bad weather, rescue officials said.

data.title: Myanmar government accuses its own UN envoy of 'illegal activities'
data.description: Myanmar's military-backed ⁠government said ⁠on Sunday its ​permanent representative to the United Nations was undertaking "illegal activities" ​and that his status had ‌been revoked and withdrawn.

data.title: Venezuelans outside Caracas say capital not sharing blackout burden
data.description: SAN CRISTOBAL (VENEZUELA) - Josner Herrera is sick and tired of dealing with daily power cuts, especially when her part of western Venezuela produces a fair bit of electricity.
